metadata.title: DryRun: See What an AI's Command Will Do
metadata.persona: Pavithra Prasad, first person (synthetic Kokoro voice af_heart reading my script)
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: INFO 7375 Final Project Pitch Film: the assignment says 'Narrate as yourself. Do not use the instructor's name, persona, or credit line.' So the house bookends are left out; B00 is my own intro and B21 my own close.
metadata.audience: hiring managers and engineers for backend and platform roles; INFO 7375 reviewers
metadata.honesty: Pitch, not a build: nothing of DryRun exists yet. B02 shows the real screenshot of Claude's reply (claude.ai, 2026-10-11), cropped; B03 my own Terminal lines from the 13 Oct re-run of the preview test, copied exactly; B19 PR #33's real test output (re-run 2026-10-23). B05 prediction, B06 simulation, B07 decision and B09 report are constructed and labelled on screen.

skin_warnings: B00: palette=claude but the cold open is 'un-annotated' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk
B21: palette=claude but the outro is 'un-annotated' — OUTRO LAW wants ClaudeTitleOutro

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Pavithra Prasad, and I'm aiming for backend and platform engineering roles. Dry Run will be a Python command-line tool that tests an AI-suggested command on a throwaway copy, and warns when the actual changes do not match the user's request.

shot.visual_intent: Title card: my name, target role, and what DryRun will do.
shot.motion_claim: Title card: my name, target role, and what DryRun will do.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: AI assistants now suggest terminal commands, and coding agents run them. One wrong character can delete files, and reading a command is not the same as knowing what it will do.

shot.visual_intent: Four phrases build the problem; beside them the AI's workstation hands a command to your folder, and the files leave it.
shot.motion_claim: Four phrases build the problem; beside them the AI's workstation hands a command to your folder, and the files leave it.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: On October eleventh, I asked Claude for a command to delete log files older than seven days. It gave me this, and told me to preview it first.

shot.visual_intent: REAL SCREENSHOT chip; the real screenshot, cropped: my request, then Claude's command outlined and its preview advice underlined as they are spoken.
shot.motion_claim: REAL SCREENSHOT chip; the real screenshot, cropped: my request, then Claude's command outlined and its preview advice underlined as they are spoken.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.
qc.contrast_reason: Real dark-mode claude.ai screenshot (evidence/claude-reply-2026-10-11.png), shown unaltered. Its dark-grey bubble on a near-black page is interface, not text. Each region that holds text is checked on its own; every region must pass and all other checks still run.

beats.narration_text: I tested the preview on a test folder on my Mac. A file seven and a half days old wasn't matched, even though it's older than seven days.

shot.visual_intent: MY TERMINAL chip; my own Terminal lines from 13 Oct, copied exactly; three file rows by age; the 7.5-day row is marked as missed.
shot.motion_claim: MY TERMINAL chip; my own Terminal lines from 13 Oct, copied exactly; three file rows by age; the 7.5-day row is marked as missed.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be a GitHub repository with tests and an evaluation report.

shot.visual_intent: The artifact: GitHub repository, tests, evaluation report; drawing: your folder and its throwaway copy; design goal: real files never touched.
shot.motion_claim: The artifact: GitHub repository, tests, evaluation report; drawing: your folder and its throwaway copy; design goal: real files never touched.

beats.narration_text: The AI will have to answer in a fixed format: the command, plus its own prediction of what that command will change.

shot.visual_intent: Example step 1: command card and predicted-changes card (constructed example).
shot.motion_claim: Example step 1: command card and predicted-changes card (constructed example).

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Dry Run will run the command on the copy, inside a locked container with no network. Then it will compare every file before and after: what was created, changed, or deleted.

shot.visual_intent: Example step 2 (constructed simulation): planned locked container; before/after file list; the 8.5-day file struck out.
shot.motion_claim: Example step 2 (constructed simulation): planned locked container; before/after file list; the 8.5-day file struck out.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It will check the real changes against the AI's prediction and the task's rules. Then it will allow, warn, or block. When it can't tell, it will say so.

shot.visual_intent: Example step 3: predicted 2 vs simulated 1; the task rule; drawing: the gate with ALLOW / WARN / BLOCK, WARN chosen.
shot.motion_claim: Example step 3: predicted 2 vs simulated 1; the task rule; drawing: the gate with ALLOW / WARN / BLOCK, WARN chosen.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: In a later phase, a blocked command's changes will go back to the AI, which will try again, up to three times.

shot.visual_intent: Later phase: changes go back to the AI; retry up to 3 times.
shot.motion_claim: Later phase: changes go back to the AI; retry up to 3 times.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: A hiring manager will be able to clone the repo, run a demo, and see the command, its predicted changes, and the real file differences. The tests and report will show where it works and where it fails.

shot.visual_intent: Example step 4: the report card (constructed mock-up) with the decision WARN, 1 file missed.
shot.motion_claim: Example step 4: the report card (constructed mock-up) with the decision WARN, 1 file missed.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: To catch mistakes like that on purpose, I'll build trap folders: names with spaces, names that look like options, hidden files, files right at a time limit, and links that point outside.

shot.visual_intent: Trap-folder file chips appear as each is named.
shot.motion_claim: Trap-folder file chips appear as each is named.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Then I'll measure it: tasks with known correct results, across every trap folder, comparing Claude with a free local model, and counting how often a command did too much or too little.

shot.visual_intent: Evaluation plan; a queue of tasks with known answers; empty counters marked NOT MEASURED YET.
shot.motion_claim: Evaluation plan; a queue of tasks with known answers; empty counters marked NOT MEASURED YET.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: A tool called try already lets developers preview a command's file changes on Linux. Research benchmarks score AI commands offline.

shot.visual_intent: Two alternatives, one prop each: a checkpoint scanner for try, an evidence binder for the research benchmarks.
shot.motion_claim: Two alternatives, one prop each: a checkpoint scanner for try, an evidence binder for the research benchmarks.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Dry Run will go one step further. It will compare the changes with your request and the AI's own prediction, and flag mismatches before you press Enter.

shot.visual_intent: What DryRun adds, in three phrases.
shot.motion_claim: What DryRun adds, in three phrases.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Together, that will show the skills from this course: a prompt contract, verification that doesn't trust the AI's explanation, an agent loop, and an evaluation you can rerun. A reviewer could fairly conclude that I can check an AI's work and measure how often it's wrong, not that Dry Run makes commands safe.

shot.visual_intent: Four skill chips appear as each is named; then the fair conclusion beside a review desk the evidence is brought to, and what is not claimed.
shot.motion_claim: Four skill chips appear as each is named; then the fair conclusion beside a review desk the evidence is brought to, and what is not claimed.

beats.narration_text: It will only check files and folders. Network calls, outside services, and databases are out of scope. The first piece I'll make run: one command, on one copied folder, listing what changed. You'll know it ran when its self-test finds exactly the changes it planted.

shot.visual_intent: In scope (a folder), out of scope, first piece, and how you will know it ran: a test bench where the self-test plants a sample.
shot.motion_claim: In scope (a folder), out of scope, first piece, and how you will know it ran: a test bench where the self-test plants a sample.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The hardest part will be knowing what you meant. I'll start with a small set of file tasks where the right result can be checked, and report uncertainty instead of guessing.

shot.visual_intent: The main risk and the plan; an inspection lamp lowers onto one checkable task.
shot.motion_claim: The main risk and the plan; an inspection lamp lowers onto one checkable task.

qc.sparse_reason: Week 1-style phrase layout on a cream stage: short phrases timed to the narration, one drawing only where it explains the mechanism. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Another risk: my Mac's command-line tools differ from Linux tools, so the first version will target Linux behaviour.

beats.narration_text: I picked Dry Run to make my portfolio stronger. I've built web apps before, but nothing that checks an AI's work.

shot.visual_intent: Why this project; my portfolio shelf and the empty slot beside it.
shot.motion_claim: Why this project; my portfolio shelf and the empty slot beside it.

beats.narration_text: Python and testing I already know, from my internship and from my Reallocation Engine pull request, which has thirty-two passing tests. I've used Docker in a cloud project at Northeastern. Sandboxing, file diffing, and evaluation design are new to me, so this is mostly new learning.

shot.visual_intent: Already know, backed by PR #33's real test output, vs new to me.
